title: Only 10% Can Pass This Grammar Quiz
summary: Explore Grammar Check-In, Sentence Builder, Precision Pass, Grammar Trapdoors, Final Proof across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: Grammar Check-In, Sentence Builder, Precision Pass, Grammar Trapdoors, Final Proof. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This quiz is not a formal English-language assessment, academic qualification or proof of language proficiency.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

insights.overview: Your grammar score at a glance

grammar-r2q3.question: Although the rain stopped ___ the path remained slippery. What belongs in the gap?

grammar-r10q1.question: Which sentence has correct subject–verb agreement?

answers.a1: The list of ingredients are on the counter.
answers.a2: The list of ingredients is on the counter.
answers.a3: The list of ingredients have been placed on the counter.
answers.a4: The list of ingredients were left beside the sink.

grammar-r1q1.question: Which option is a complete sentence?

answers.a1: After the final paragraph
answers.a2: The editor checked the final paragraph.
answers.a3: Because the deadline changed
answers.a4: While everyone was waiting

grammar-r1q3.context: The notes belong to several students.
grammar-r1q3.question: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?

answers.a1: The students’ notes were organised.
answers.a2: The student’s notes were organised.
answers.a3: The students notes’ were organised.
answers.a4: The students note’s were organised.

grammar-r1q4.context: Nora thanked Priya after Priya corrected the caption.
grammar-r1q4.question: Which revision makes the reference clearest?

answers.a1: Nora thanked her after she corrected it.
answers.a2: She thanked Priya after she corrected it.
answers.a3: Nora thanked Priya for correcting the caption.
answers.a4: Nora thanked Priya after it was corrected by her.

grammar-r1q5.question: Which wording is the clearest and most concise?

answers.a1: The report is concise in a clear manner.
answers.a2: The report is concise and clear.
answers.a3: The report has clarity and is concise in nature.
answers.a4: The report is being of a concise and clear kind.

grammar-r3q1.question: The meeting began at 09:00. Leo finished the chart at 08:30. Which sentence is correct?

answers.a1: Leo completed the chart after the meeting began.
answers.a2: Leo had completed the chart after the meeting began.
answers.a3: Leo has completed the chart before the meeting began.
answers.a4: Leo had completed the chart before the meeting began.

grammar-r4q3.question: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?

answers.a1: The file was large; because it loaded slowly.
answers.a2: The file was large; it loaded slowly.
answers.a3: The file was large, it loaded slowly.
answers.a4: The file was large; although it loaded slowly.

grammar-r3q2.context: Asha started at the library on Monday and still works there now.
grammar-r3q2.question: Which sentence matches the timeline?

answers.a1: Asha worked at the library since Monday.
answers.a2: Asha has worked at the library since Monday.
answers.a3: Asha had worked at the library since Monday, but still does.
answers.a4: Asha is work at the library since Monday.

grammar-r3q5.context: The clause “which won the award” must describe the documentary, not the director.
grammar-r3q5.question: Which sentence attaches the clause clearly?

answers.a1: The director, which won the award, introduced the documentary.
answers.a2: The director introduced, which won the award, the documentary.
answers.a3: Which won the award, the director introduced the documentary.
answers.a4: The director introduced the documentary, which won the award.

grammar-r3q6.question: Which sentence uses a reflexive pronoun correctly?

answers.a1: The technicians completed the review by theirselves.
answers.a2: The technicians completed the review by themselves.
answers.a3: The technicians completed the review by themself.
answers.a4: The technicians completed themselves the review.

grammar-r4q1.question: Which sentence introduces the list correctly?

answers.a1: Bring three items: a notebook, a pen and identification.
answers.a2: Bring: three items a notebook, a pen and identification.
answers.a3: Bring three: items, a notebook a pen and identification.
answers.a4: Bring three items; a notebook, a pen and identification.

grammar-r5q4.context: Between Lina and ___, this decision must remain confidential.
grammar-r5q4.question: Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?

answers.a1: me
answers.a2: I
answers.a3: my
answers.a4: mine

grammar-r10q4.question: Several chefs share these lockers. Which sign is written correctly?

answers.a1: The chefs lockers
answers.a2: The chef's lockers
answers.a3: The chefs' lockers
answers.a4: The chefs's lockers

grammar-r5q1.context: The policy has two sections. The second section contains the deadline.
grammar-r5q1.question: Which revision refers to the deadline most clearly?

answers.a1: It contains it in the second one.
answers.a2: The policy has two sections, and it contains the deadline.
answers.a3: The deadline appears in the policy’s second section.
answers.a4: The second has it, which is in the policy.

grammar-r5q5.question: Which option is a complete, correctly ordered sentence?

answers.a1: Because the labels were missing.
answers.a2: The labels, because missing, the boxes.
answers.a3: The boxes were delayed because the labels were missing.
answers.a4: The boxes because the labels were missing delayed.

grammar-r5q6.question: Which sentence correctly punctuates a direct address?

answers.a1: Ravi please, check the final line.
answers.a2: Ravi, please check the final line.
answers.a3: Ravi please check, the final line.
answers.a4: Ravi; please, check the final line.

grammar-r6q1.context: Only the blue folders were archived; the other folders remained active.
grammar-r6q1.question: Which sentence preserves that restriction?

answers.a1: The folders were archived blue only.
answers.a2: Only the folders were archived in blue.
answers.a3: The folders only were archived blue.
answers.a4: Only the blue folders were archived.

answers.a1: Visitors must sign in, wearing a badge and return it before leaving.
answers.a2: Visitors must sign in, wear a badge and return it before leaving.
answers.a3: Visitors must sign in, wear a badge and returning it before leaving.
answers.a4: Visitors must sign in, to wear a badge and return it before leaving.

grammar-r9q5.question: Only the first report was revised. Which sentence makes that meaning unambiguous?

answers.a1: Only the editor revised the first report.
answers.a2: The editor revised the first report only to correct the title.
answers.a3: The editor revised the first report only yesterday.
answers.a4: The editor revised only the first report.

trapdoorErrors.a1: only changes who performed the action
trapdoorErrors.a2: the purpose phrase changes why the report was revised
trapdoorErrors.a3: only changes when the action happened

grammar-r7q3.context:
PARAGRAPH
The room was ready. Except for the missing chairs. The guests arrived at noon.
grammar-r7q3.question: Which edit removes the fragment?

answers.a1: The room was ready except for the missing chairs. The guests arrived at noon.
answers.a2: The room was ready. Except the missing chairs were. The guests arrived.
answers.a3: The room. Was ready except for missing chairs, guests arrived.
answers.a4: Except for the missing chairs. The room was ready and at noon.

grammar-r7q4.context: The intended meaning is that the speaker answered nearly every question.
grammar-r7q4.question: Which wording expresses that meaning?

answers.a1: The speaker answered every nearly question.
answers.a2: Nearly the speaker answered every question.
answers.a3: The speaker nearly answered every question.
answers.a4: The speaker answered nearly every question.

grammar-r7q6.context: A report contains a summary and an appendix. The appendix is updated monthly.
grammar-r7q6.question: Which edit makes the monthly update refer to the appendix?

answers.a1: The report contains a summary and an appendix, and it is updated monthly.
answers.a2: The report contains a summary, which is updated monthly, and an appendix.
answers.a3: The report contains a summary and an appendix; the appendix is updated monthly.
answers.a4: The report, updated monthly, contains a summary and its appendix.

grammar-r9q1.question: Which sentence handles the contrast correctly?

answers.a1: The storm ended; although the streets remained flooded.
answers.a2: The storm ended, however the streets remained flooded.
answers.a3: Although the storm ended; the streets remained flooded.
answers.a4: Although the storm ended, the streets remained flooded.

trapdoorErrors.a1: semicolon incorrectly separates a main clause from a dependent clause
trapdoorErrors.a2: conjunctive adverb lacks the required boundary punctuation
trapdoorErrors.a3: semicolon incorrectly follows a dependent clause

visual.ariaLabel: The final reports were checked before the editor approve them

answers.a1: A
answers.a2: B
answers.a3: C
answers.a4: D

answers.a1: After reviewing the figures, Maya confirmed that each total was accurate.
answers.a2: After reviewing the figures, each total was confirmed by Maya.
answers.a3: After reviewing the figures, Maya confirm that each total was accurate.
answers.a4: After reviewing the figures, Maya confirmed that each of the totals were accurate.

answers.a1: The doors opened, but nobody entered.
answers.a2: The doors opened, nobody entered.
answers.a3: Although the doors opened, but nobody entered.
answers.a4: The doors opened but. Nobody entered.

grammar-r8q3.context: The handle belongs to one door.
grammar-r8q3.question: Choose the correct apostrophe.

answers.a1: the doors handle
answers.a2: the doors’ handle
answers.a3: the door’s handle
answers.a4: the door’ handle

answers.a1: The designers prepared the display by theirselves.
answers.a2: The designers prepared the display by themselves.
answers.a3: The designers prepared the display by themself.
answers.a4: The designers prepared the display by theirs.

grammar-r8q5.context: The number almost doubled but did not quite reach twice its original size.
grammar-r8q5.question: Which wording matches?

answers.a1: The update nearly doubled the number.
answers.a2: The update doubled nearly the number.
answers.a3: Nearly the update doubled the number.
answers.a4: The update doubled the nearly number.
